text: Throughout the program lifecycle, and knowing that stakeholder engagement is critical to program success, the program manager works constantly to engage stakeholders and gain their support. You are the program manager for a multi-tier program ranging across multiple stakeholder channels and a wide range of stakeholders’ groups. Which of the below is the best way to communicate with stakeholders?

You noticed that your program manager had issues with monitoring and controlling the schedule of her project which was clearly noticeable due to the multiple delays she faced recently; you approached your project manager and gave her a suggestion, however, she delayed the decision which further delayed the schedule. What should be your next course of action?
choices: A. Fire her and put another competent project manager instead
B. Escalate the issue with the project manager to the sponsor

text: Stakeholders are engaged throughout the course of the program in order to ensure that the program successfully delivers its benefits. A program manager maintains a stakeholder register and continuously revises it in order to ensure correct and timely stakeholder engagement. Which of the below is part of the content of a stakeholder register?

Contracts are signed and related work is initiated throughout the program lifecycle. Contracts are normally administered at component level and the program manager maintains oversight on the financial expenditure of a contract and on its closure requests. Which of the below lists the correct steps of closing a contract?
choices: A. There are no outstanding contractual issues, deliverables have been satisfactorily completed, all payments have been made,
B. All payments have been made, deliverables have been satisfactorily completed, there are no outstanding contractual issues
C. Deliverables have been satisfactorily completed, all payments have been made, there are no outstanding contractual issues
D. Deliverables have been satisfactorily completed, budget is closed, all payments have been made, there are no outstanding contractual issues

text: Program manager spends a good amount of time preparing the schedule. From the scope statement, the program manager derives the PWBS which will help in the make-or-buy decisions, and in estimating the cost, quality, resource and duration. To what level should the PWBS be decomposed?
choices: B. Until it reaches the work packages
D. Only to show the program packages

text: Throughout the course of the program, the program manager works to realize benefits within the constraints he has. Benefits are being continuously defined, revised, monitored and controlled. You have done benefits identification, defined critical success factors and developed a benefits register. Which of the below is part of the content of a benefits register?
choices: A. Benefit ID, details, expected improvement start date, expected target achievement date, target value, benefit realization constraint
B. Benefit ID, details, stakeholders affected by the benefit, target value, benefit realization constraint, benefit progress
C. Benefit ID, details, expected funding date, expected return on investment, target value, benefit realization constraint
D. Benefit ID, details, alternative approaches, target value, benefit realization constraint

text: Your company has acquired company B and multiple projects were transferred from company B to your program. The project managers are not reporting in the format required by your program and even you have met with them regularly and informed them of the need for a unified reporting, they refuse to comply. What should be your next action?
choices: A. Request the PMO to include company B reporting standards to your program
B. You have no other option but to comply to them and modify their reports to your needs
C. Use forced communication and inform them that strict actions will be taken in case of non-compliance
D. Do nothing and continue as planned

text: Throughout the program lifecycle, and knowing that stakeholder engagement is critical to program success, the program manager works constantly to engage stakeholders and gain their support. You are the program manager for a multi-tier program ranging across multiple stakeholder channels and a wide range of stakeholders’ groups. From the below options, which are considered as key stakeholders?
choices: B. Legal department manager, component managers, competitors
C. Program management team, component managers, media consultants
D. Program management team, family members, sponsors

text: Throughout the program lifecycle, the program manager works constantly to engage stakeholders and gain their support. You are the program manager for a multi-tier program ranging across multiple stakeholder channels and a wide range of stakeholders’ groups. Throughout the program, you realize that stakeholders have different and/or contradicting views of the program objectives. You have reached a point where everyone is happy; however, you needed to negotiate on multiple points and compromise on others. You performed these activities as part of

You have good relations with your customer and you are managing a program for him. The customer doesn’t require you to send him performance reviews as he believes that you can manage to deliver a successful program. What should you do in this case?
choices: A. Don’t send performance reviews because the customer requested it
B. Send the performance reviews as planned
C. Consult your steering committee for advice
D. Consult your sponsor for advice

text: You have been newly assigned to manage a program to implement a new software system across the entire enterprise in all of its branches. You identify organizational benefits for the potential program using research methods such as market analysis and high level cost-benefit analysis in order to develop?
choices: D. Preliminary program scope and define benefits realization plan

text: At closure, a lot of stakeholders have changed since the beginning and board members changed as well; a new board member just joined the company and has vague understanding of her roles and responsibilities. What should you do in this case?
choices: A. Show her the benefit management plan
B. Show her the governance plan
C. Update the governance plan to include the new stakeholder

text: You have successfully reached to the closure phase of your program to deliver a drug that will cure cancer instantly around the world. You have also transitioned the program to operational entities in the company and are currently conducting the review meeting. Which of the below is an output of post review meetings?
choices: A. Obtain feedback and capture lessons learned
C. Make sure procurements are closed

text: You have successfully reached to the closure phase of your program to deliver a drug that will cure cancer instantly around the world. You have closed all components and related contracts. You have just got stakeholders approval for closure, what do you do next?
choices: C. PMIS archival and resource disposition

text: Programs deliver the intended benefits fully at closure or incrementally throughout the delivery phase. Some programs realize full benefits and others have to transition the program to operational entities to ensure the realization of benefits on the long run. If your program is based on incremental deliveries, what do you do with components after they deliver the intended benefits?
choices: A. Leave them open until program closure phase where they will be closed
B. Close them after delivering their outputs
C. Transition them without closure until reaching the closure phase
D. Put them on hold until the resources are no longer needed

text: Your program to deliver a new metro easing the life of the residents and decreasing travel time due to the busy city streets has begun. You are preparing a business case and you have already ensured the strategic alignment with organization and have performed a feasibility study; what else do you need to do?
choices: B. Develop a high level milestone plan

text: You have been assigned by the sponsor to manage a high priority program in your organization. The program is already in its planning phase and the previous manager has retired. The planning phase spans a full year and is considered critical to the successful delivery of a program. As a first step, which document you study?

You have been assigned by the sponsor to manage a high priority program in your organization. The program is already in its delivery phase and the previous manager has retired. The delivery is already mid-way and the program is being delivered as planned. As a first step, which document you study?

You have been working hard in the delivery phase of your program to build a new metro station in order to reduce the travel time between two cities and so far, you have managed to stay on track. An electrical shutdown occurred in the city and the operation stopped for two days with a loss of $150k and a slight delay in schedule. What should you do?
choices: D. Analyze impact and approve change request

text: You are starting to prepare a business case for a program and the sponsor informed you that the company is undergoing budget cuts due to financial difficulties and your program might not be fully funded. What must you do in this case?
choices: A. Prepare an initial risk assessment
C. Estimate the high-level ﬁnancial and non-ﬁnancial beneﬁts

text: Funding differs between programs and between different components of a program. The funding organization may impose limitations which will be considered as constraints in the planning. One of your program components is funded externally, which of the below is correct?
choices: A. Programs can be funded externally but components can’t
B. Components can be funded externally but programs can’t
C. Both components and programs can be funded externally
D. Both components and programs can’t be funded externally

text: A program manager maintains a close look on the program benefits throughout the program lifecycle. Governance board is also focused on delivering benefits and conduct regular meetings to ensure it. Benefits are the most important assets of a program and you constantly work to realize them. Early in your program, you have prepared a benefits management plan in order to guide benefits delivery, and guide benefits monitoring and controlling throughout the course of the program. Which of the below represents the performance baseline of a program?

You have been assigned as the program manager to manage the release of five new ice cream flavors within the next year. The company is betting a lot on this program because it has been failing its last few programs and is currently facing hard times keeping up with the fast growing market. During the course of the program, a risk occurred, which is above your authority level. Which of the below is the correct action to take?
choices: A. You record it and assign a member to follow up on it
B. You record it, analyze it and recommend change to steering committee
C. You directly escalate to steering committee
D. You communicate it with all stakeholders

text: Different stakeholders have different interests, expectations and needs. Some data is confidential for a certain group of stakeholders while being authorized for others. Program manager needs to maintain communication targeted to each stakeholder or stakeholder groups. You are starting a program to build a new cars line for your client that will be more fuel efficient and has more safety features. From the below, which option lists key stakeholders?
choices: A. Car dealers, component managers and sponsors
B. Customers, legal and executive management
C. Component managers, media consultants and customer

text: You have prepared a performance report and presented the above to steering committee. Having looked at these numbers, which of the below is true?
choices: A. Program is over budget and ahead of schedule
B. Program is over budget and behind schedule
C. Component A is under budget and behind schedule
D. Component C is over budget and ahead of schedule
